title: thynC remote central monitor flags ventricular tachycardia at 192 bpm in an 85-year-old on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital; staff resuscitate the patient within the golden time (14 January 2026)
summary: thynC alarm flagged ventricular tachycardia in an 85-year-old on a Gwangju general ward; staff CPR restored circulation, 14 January 2026.
account: On 14 January 2026 at about 3:10 p.m., an 85-year-old patient's heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute. The patient was on a general ward of Gwangju Hanguk Hospital (광주한국병원) in Gwangju, South Korea. thynC had monitored the patient since 9 January because of cardiovascular risk factors at admission. thynC's remote central monitor flagged ventricular tachycardia, a precursor sign of cardiac arrest, and alarmed. Staff who ran to the room found seizure-like movements, reduced consciousness and no spontaneous breathing. They performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and artificial respiration. The heartbeat and circulation returned, and the patient was moved to intensive care. Daewoong Pharmaceutical, which supplies thynC, announced the case on 11 February 2026 with statements from the hospital's directors and nursing manager.
purpose: The hospital and Daewoong Pharmaceutical describe thynC as an AI-based smart bed monitoring system. It measures electrocardiogram (ECG), heart rate and respiratory rate through wearable devices. It sends an alarm to a central monitor when an abnormal sign appears. So patients on a general ward, where staff cannot stay at every bedside, are watched in real time as in an intensive care unit. Staff can respond early to deterioration. Flagging a pre-arrest arrhythmia and summoning staff is exactly that design. Daewoong's hospital-division head describes thynC as built to recognize changes in a patient's condition early and help medical staff respond quickly.
system: thynC (씽크) AI-based smart bed monitoring system: wearable sensors measuring ECG, heart rate and respiratory rate in real time, with alarms sent to a remote central monitor
developer: Not stated in the read reports, which describe thynC as the smart bed monitoring system that Daewoong Pharmaceutical supplies (자사 공급)

ratings.reason: The hospital reports that the alarm brought staff to a patient in ventricular tachycardia who had stopped breathing. It reports that CPR within the golden time restored heartbeat and circulation, and that the patient went to intensive care. The hospital calls this averting a cardiac-arrest crisis. But survival to discharge and neurological outcome are not reported. The account was released by the system's supplier. So a life saved is not established.

ai_role.statement: The system's contribution was detection and summons. The wearable ECG stream showed the heart rate climbing to 192 beats per minute. The remote central monitor identified ventricular tachycardia and raised an alarm. The attending director says that is how staff learned of it at once and reached the bedside to begin CPR within the golden time. The resuscitation itself was done by people. The counterfactual rests on the hospital's framing that general-ward patients are not under continuous observation and that deterioration can be noticed late. How long this patient would otherwise have gone unobserved is not recorded. No medical record or independent assessment has been published. The case reached the press through a Daewoong Pharmaceutical announcement of 11 February 2026.

produced_by: thynC wearable monitoring of ECG, heart rate and respiratory rate, linked to a remote central monitor on a general ward. It started on 9 January 2026 because the patient had cardiovascular risk factors at admission
An alarm raised the moment the heart rate climbed to 192 beats per minute and the monitor identified ventricular tachycardia

Ward staff who went to the bedside on the alarm and performed CPR and artificial respiration within the golden time. The reports put that time at four minutes for acute cardiac arrest, citing National Fire Agency data
must_hold: The case reached the press through a Daewoong Pharmaceutical announcement of 11 February 2026. The hospital's attending director, chief director and nursing manager are quoted. But no medical record, case report or independent review has been published
Only the return of heartbeat and circulation and the transfer to intensive care are reported. Survival to discharge and neurological outcome are not

The alarm shortens the time to detection, not the treatment. The benefit depends on staff who can reach the bedside and resuscitate within minutes. The nursing manager says that is hardest to guarantee at night and when staffing is thin

headline: thynC flags ventricular tachycardia; CPR restores circulation
metric: a heart rate that climbed to 192 beats per minute

later.note: Daewoong completed thynC installations covering 558 beds at Chonnam National University Hospital and Hwasun Chonnam National University Hospital, the largest national-university-hospital deployment so far, among several 2026 hospital rollouts.
later.quote: 총 558병상 규모(전남대병원 217병상·화순전남대병원 341병상)로 진행된 이번 사업은 국립대병원 최대 규모의 씽크 구축 사례로, 호남권 상급종합병원의 스마트병동 전환을 본격화하는 계기가 될 것으로 회사는 기대한다.
